records.text: Clump: a bulky mass of human-like limbs adapted to cramped spaces such as vents, pipes, cabinets and narrow recesses. It commonly hunts from concealment, remaining still until prey comes close, then rapidly extending one or more long arms to seize, immobilize and drag the victim toward its central mass or into the confined space where it is hiding. When forced to move it can be unexpectedly fast and can use its many limbs to climb or traverse vents. External references agree on the limb-cluster appearance, close-range ambush/grab tactic and confined-space preference, but disagree on exact reach and speed, so no hard numeric range is canon here. Project hard lock applies: a Clump is never friendly or neutral toward humans.

records.text: Duller: a tall, elongated dark-gray humanoid with long arms, an unnatural or frail-looking frame and no normal human facial features. External references agree that it can no-clip part of its body through solid walls, especially an arm, to seize prey on the opposite side and drag the victim away; despite its thin appearance it can move quickly and exert substantial strength. External sources conflict on overt behavior: one describes direct avoidance outside its wall-ambush tactic while another describes active stalking and hostility. Project canon therefore resolves only the gameplay boundary, not the disputed behavior: a Duller is never friendly or neutral toward humans, and apparent withdrawal must not be treated as safety. Hallucination/gas abilities, exact body variants and exact reach remain uncommitted because they are not consistently corroborated across the checked sources.

records.text: Deathmoth: a large moth-like insectoid predator with scaled membranous wings, prominent antennae and clawed segmented legs; exact body size and caste anatomy vary across external references, so no single numeric form is locked here. Project canon takes precedence: encountered Deathmoths are hostile predators that use dark ceilings and technical recesses, often attack in groups, react to light and movement, and on Level 3 can exploit broken-light zones to pressure humans toward live electrical hazards. External references additionally corroborate coordinated swarm attacks and corrosive ejecta in aggressive variants, used to injure or incapacitate prey before feeding or transporting organic matter. Older external material describes some males as harmless or tamable; that directly conflicts with ENTITY.GLOBAL_HARD_LOCK and is not canon in this game. Do not infer that a quieter individual is safe, and do not assign archived hive/caste rules to every encounter unless current game state establishes them.

records.text: Smiler: a hostile presence most reliably identified in darkness by bright reflective or glowing eyes and a wide grin of visible sharp teeth; the rest of its body is not reliably established and should remain visually uncommitted unless directly observed. Project canon takes precedence: Smilers use blacked-out areas and dark corners and may keep distance to pressure prey into choosing a bad route instead of charging immediately. External references consistently associate them with light attraction and escalation when prey panics, retreats abruptly or makes loud noise; once committed, they can chase or lunge from darkness. Eye contact and slow controlled withdrawal are reported survival tactics, but they are not absolute guarantees. External sources disagree on whether Smilers literally lack a body or whether direct light destroys them, so neither claim is canon here. ENTITY.GLOBAL_HARD_LOCK applies even when a Smiler appears stationary or merely watches.
